clue.text: Took down a peg

parts.note: reads as humbled someone, but a peg is also a tot of spirits, so taking one down means drinking it

explanation.definitionFit: Gulping a drink of spirits down the throat is exactly what the cryptic reading describes.

clue.text: Cancel loan when creditor intervenes

indicators.note: the creditor's letters come between the letters of the loan word, intervening in it

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan of money, as against wages

explanation.surface: A lender steps in and a loan is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan or arrangement is informally to call it off.

clue.text: Girl has hat it crawls along

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A girl wears a hat with something creeping along it.
explanation.definitionFit: An annelid is a segmented worm, a creature that moves by crawling.

clue.text: Perfectly executed, but in an uncontrolled way

indicators.note: executed here means beheaded, so the word for perfectly loses its first letter

parts.note: flawlessly means perfectly, without a single fault

explanation.surface: Something was done perfectly yet also wildly out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfectly executed' looks like praise for a performance; 'executed' actually cuts the head (F) off FLAWLESSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without regard for rules or restraint is behaving without law.

clue.text: Ace shooter, a foreigner, involved in Millwall tie

indicators.note: involved suggests twisted or entangled, so the letters of the football fixture are rearranged

parts.note: Millwall is a London football club; a tie is a cup match

explanation.surface: A crack marksman from abroad turns up at a Millwall cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: MILLWALL TIE, the anagram fodder, has exactly the eleven letters needed; Millwall is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss folk hero famed for shooting an apple off his son's head was a superb marksman and, to the British, a foreigner.

clue.text: Drops of water joined up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for joined is read from bottom to top

parts.note: wed means joined in marriage

explanation.surface: Drops of water came together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew is moisture condensed in small beads on surfaces overnight.

clue.text: Missing books, jealous Shakespearian gives cry of surprise

indicators.note: missing means the books are dropped out of the name of the jealous hero

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's jealous Moor
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A jealous Shakespearian character, missing some books, cries out in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello can be an exclamation of surprise, as in 'hello, what's this?'

clue.text: Is in charge of latrine

definitions.meaning: to head something is to lead or run it
on a ship the toilets are called the ...

explanation.definitionFit: One who leads a body runs it; sailors call shipboard toilets by the same word.

clue.text: Comic attempt to extend one's support?

definitions.meaning: a hoax or teasing joke played on someone
read literally, stretching the limb one stands on

explanation.definitionFit: A tease is a joking attempt to fool someone; literally, drawing out a limb that holds you up.

clue.text: Old writer stopped employing undefined term

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
ended means stopped or finished

explanation.surface: An old author gave up using a vague expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A period with no fixed finish date is unlimited, with no limits defined.

clue.text: Genuine case for fresh extension of loan

indicators.note: the word for genuine acts as a case, enclosing the word for fresh

parts.note: real means genuine
new means fresh

explanation.surface: A real reason to extend a loan again.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing a loan for a further period is renewing it.

clue.text: Row beyond water margins to fish

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Rowing out past the water's edge to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a boat, but it is a quarrel; 'beyond' just links W R, the first and last letters of 'water', to ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a noisy argument or dispute.

clue.text: Backing point with plausible nonsense

indicators.note: backing means the word for plausible is read backwards

parts.note: glib means plausible in a smooth, shallow way
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Smooth-talking support for a point that is actually rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for rubbish talk, from the foul water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Unsettled side put in for a transfer

indicators.note: a transfer moves things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A football side, unsettled, is put up for a transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter being argued over is not yet decided or resolved.

clue.text: Only pretend to embrace since break up

indicators.note: the word for pretending hugs the word for since inside it

parts.note: to dissemble is to put on a false appearance
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: Someone only pretends to hug, since they are splitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a machine is to take it to pieces.

clue.text: Into which teacher finally collapses?

parts.note: the place a tired teacher drops into at the end of the day; a teacher's degree is also the Bachelor of Education

explanation.surface: An exhausted teacher flops down at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The furniture one sleeps in is where anyone worn out finally drops.

clue.text: Spread round the opposite of Johnson's advice on second marriages?

definitions.meaning: scattered about, as petals over a path

definitions.text: the opposite of Johnson's advice on second marriages?
definitions.meaning: Dr Johnson called remarriage the triumph of hope over experience; the opposite advice would be that one is best married again

explanation.definitionFit: Scattered over a surface describes strewn things; split differently the letters say marrying again is best.

clue.text: Not qualified as craftsmen, but get houses finished

parts.note: semis are semi-detached houses
finished off means killed

explanation.surface: Unskilled workers nonetheless manage to finish building some houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers with some training but not a full trade are partly trained.

clue.text: No art in this subject of Blake's songs?

definitions.text: No art in this subject of Blake's songs?

parts.words: No art in this subject of Blake's songs?
parts.note: artlessness, a lack of guile, is the theme of the first half of William Blake's paired song collections

explanation.definitionFit: Being without art in the sense of cunning is a state of purity, the theme Blake set against Experience.

clue.text: No news, then, of foolish boy that crossed the water

indicators.note: the foolish boy is split open with the water lying across the middle

parts.note: silly means foolish
a son is a boy
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A tale of a daft lad who crossed the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The summer lull when newspapers fill pages with trivia because nothing important happens.

clue.text: Prescribe sacrifice

definitions.meaning: to set down rules, as in laying down the law
to give up, as in laying down one's life

explanation.definitionFit: To dictate rules is to establish them; giving up one's life is to surrender it.

clue.text: No credit for swimmer

definitions.meaning: cash on delivery, payment made on receipt rather than on account

explanation.definitionFit: Cash on delivery means paying at once rather than on account; also a familiar white-fleshed fish.

clue.text: Be on good terms with previous husband — one's in bed

indicators.note: in places the husband and the one's inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
an ex is a former husband
I'S, one is, with I as the Roman one

explanation.surface: Getting along with your ex-husband when he is in your bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To live side by side peacefully is to exist together without conflict.

clue.text: Label your work in vivid hue

indicators.note: work as a verb suggests reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to label one's work in a bright colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep bright shade associated with the monarchy is a striking colour.

clue.text: I'm standing in line, being an Englishman

indicators.note: the I'm stands inside the word for line

parts.note: a ley is a line, as in ley lines

explanation.surface: I'm queuing, being English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing in line' is the British queue; LEY is a line as in ley lines. Limey is American slang for a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a Briton, from limes given to sailors against scurvy.

clue.text: Jump over net

definitions.meaning: to ... a fence is to leap it

explanation.definitionFit: To leap a hurdle cleanly is to clear it; money remaining after deductions is clear profit.

clue.text: I heard you, boy

definitions.meaning: radio procedure word for message received

explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators acknowledge a message with this word; it is also a man's name.

clue.text: Holding party in turn, female may need him for a spruce cut

indicators.note: the word for female holds the reversed party inside it

parts.note: a woman is a female

indicators.note: in turn means the word for party is turned round

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A woman holding a party may need a man to give a smart haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce cut' suggests a smart haircut; spruce is the tree a forester fells.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester fells trees such as spruce.

clue.text: How one differs from bone-head

wordplay.reading: one has every letter of bone except the B

parts.note: compare the two words: the shorter is the longer with its opening letter missing

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a single digit differs from a bonehead.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'bone-head' hides the split: 'bone' compared with 'one' lacks B, and 'head' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nob is old slang for the head, as in a knock on the nob.

clue.text: Compulsory cover

definitions.meaning: the outer case of a book

explanation.definitionFit: A legally obligatory agreement holds the parties; a book's covers hold its pages.

clue.text: Both ends of day were fine

wordplay.reading: the first and last letters of day, D, Y, joined as both one and the other

parts.note: read literally, the phrase names the first letter and the last letter of the word day, with the and of 'both ... and' between them

explanation.surface: The days at both ends of the week were fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both ends of day' looks like dawn and dusk; read literally it is the letter D and the letter Y. 'were' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandy is an informal, slightly dated word for excellent or all right.

clue.text: Head off a licking, protected by stout bodyguard

indicators.note: the word for stout surrounds and shields the shortened word

parts.note: stout is a dark beer

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a licking is a thrashing or defeat

explanation.surface: A stout bodyguard shields someone from a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a licking' looks like a beating the bodyguard suffers, but it is a word whose head is cut off; 'stout' is the beer, not a description of the guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen Warders at the Tower of London, nicknamed thus, began as royal guards.
